classification.difficultyReason: 1G Q21: Linked familiar operations with signs, exact values or endpoint/domain checks. The coefficients give discriminant 192 and two irrational roots; the formula example supplies the same substitution and simplification sequence.

answer.short:
$x=\dfrac{2\pm\sqrt3}{4}$.

Use the quadratic formula and simplify $\sqrt{192}=8\sqrt3$.
answer.worked:
Use the quadratic formula with $a=16$, $b=-16$ and $c=1$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-(-16)\pm\sqrt{(-16)^2-4(16)(1)}}{2(16)}\\x&=\frac{16\pm\sqrt{192}}{32}\\x&=\frac{16\pm8\sqrt3}{32}\\x&=\frac{2\pm\sqrt3}{4}\end{align*}$$
